artifacts.summary: Confirms all six books-observe.sh RUN-log field-name/type mismatches against the live schema and 149-line consumer-repo log, diagnoses the existing test fixture as encoding the bug rather than the schema, and rules on a two-part fail-loud mechanism (unrecognized-schema check + permissive-vs-strict match-count divergence check) retroactively verified against mismatch 1.

memory_candidates.content: When a reader script's test fixture is built to match the reader's own (possibly wrong) field expectations rather than the normative schema document, the fixture launders the bug: it passes because it exercises the bug's own logic, not the schema. Diagnosis technique: always build/verify a reader's test fixtures directly against the schema document's Fields table, never against the reader's current parsing code, especially when auditing a reader for field-name drift.

To retroactively validate a proposed fail-loud detection mechanism for a silent-degradation bug, replay the ORIGINAL buggy logic against the mechanism and confirm it would have fired. A schema-version-field check alone does not catch a type-mismatch filter bug (the schema value itself is unaffected); pair it with a permissive-vs-strict match-count divergence check (normalize both sides with tostring for the permissive count, compare against the schema-faithful strict count) to catch exactly that class of defect without weakening the production filter itself.
